messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: multiple model-serving pods in eu-west-3 experienced host reboots and 5xx errors starting ~12:03 UTC. Autoscaler attempted reschedules; customers A and C saw increased latency/failed calls. Root symptoms: repeated PCIe AER and ECC messages in host kernel logs. Please triage and hand off as needed.

kevin_oncall: I'm on it. Initial check: control plane reports 6 pod restarts across 3 different nodes in the eu-west-3 GPU pool. No ongoing alert for host network but pod-level 503 spikes reported. Any quick mitigation suggestions?

priya_sre: Start by draining affected nodes to stop scheduled workloads, and move live traffic to eu-west-1 if capacity available. I'll pull journalctl from the node and paste relevant lines.

jamal_infra: I'm preparing a drain. Node IDs: gpu-eu3-047, gpu-eu3-052, gpu-eu3-059. Draining now: `kubectl drain gpu-eu3-047 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

priya_sre: Logs from gpu-eu3-047 (tail):
```
Mar 10 12:02:57 kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: correctable error received: rid 0000:65:00.0
Mar 10 12:02:57 kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=0000(Receiver ID)
Mar 10 12:03:01 kernel: nvidia 0000:66:00.0: GPU ECC fatal error: device stopped
Mar 10 12:03:05 kernel: pciehp 0000:65:00.0: Slot(0-1): link down
Mar 10 12:03:08 kernel: kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000010
```
Those AER lines are noisy around the reboots.

kevin_oncall: Copying. Looks like a hardware/driver-level fault causing kernel instability. Priya, can you grep for repeated AER floods and count occurrences in last hour?

priya_sre: Ran: `journalctl -k -u systemd --since "1 hour ago" | grep -i aer | wc -l` -> 137 on gpu-eu3-047, 121 on gpu-eu3-052, 8 on gpu-eu3-059. Pattern: bursty floods on .047 and .052 then host OOM/kern panic and reboot.

sasha_reliability: Hypothesis 1: Noisy neighbor / PCIe signal integrity issue on those hosts causing corrected errors to escalate to fatal ECC. Hypothesis 2: recent kernel/driver update triggered regression. Hypothesis 3: underlying fabric (top-of-rack switch) intermittently flapping and causing GPU driver to misbehave. We'll test by isolating hardware and checking firmware/driver versions.

emily_se: Customer impact for top 3 accounts during window 12:02-12:20 UTC:
- acct-A: 23% increased 5xx, 2 rolling restarts (model-serving), 45 requests failed
- acct-C: degraded latency 300ms -> 1.2s, 120 requests timed out
- internal qa: some synthetic checks failed, alerts triggered.
I opened post-incident comms draft for affected customers.

jamal_infra: Opened a GCP support case and attached kernel logs + dmesg excerpt. Case #GCP-4579123. GCP acknowledged receipt and requested the host serial and console logs. I've exported host serial logs to the case.

kevin_oncall: Mitigations executed so far: drained the three nodes, set autoscaler to prefer eu-west-1 for 1 hour, bumped replica counts to maintain capacity where possible, and added a temporary routing policy to avoid the eu-west-3 GPU pool.

priya_sre: Also applied a temporary node taint to prevent rescheduling onto the reprovisioning hosts: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-eu3-047 transient=true:NoSchedule`

sasha_reliability: For timeline:
- 12:02 UTC: First PCIe AER messages observed on gpu-eu3-047
- 12:03 UTC: Kernel panic and node reboot on gpu-eu3-047; pod restarts observed
- 12:04-12:08 UTC: Similar AER bursts on gpu-eu3-052 -> reboot
- 12:10 UTC: pod restart wave across pool -> autoscaler triggers
- 12:12 UTC: Alerts page on-call
- 12:15 UTC: Drains started; migrations to eu-west-1 started
- 12:35 UTC: GCP case opened (GCP-4579123)
- 12:48 UTC: GCP acknowledged, requested serial logs

kevin_oncall: Good timeline. Next actions: collect full kernel oops logs, stack traces for the GPU driver, and the PCIe device IDs. Priya, can you paste `lspci -vvv` output from one of affected hosts if you have it saved?

priya_sre: Extract (trimmed):
```
65:00.0 PCI bridge: Broadcom XYZ PCIe-to-PCI bridge (rev 01)
66:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA GA102 [A100] (rev a1)
66:00.1 Audio device: NVIDIA Corporation Device 1aeb
```
Bridge vendor is Broadcom on these hosts, same across the pool.

jamal_infra: Note: No kernel/driver upgrade was rolled out in the last 72 hours to this pool. Last maintenance window 5 days ago touched non-GPU drivers only.

sasha_reliability: That lowers likelihood of regression from recent package update. Focus on intermittent hardware/fabric or transient firmware issues. Next: request GCP to do host-level diagnostics and PCIe bus scans, and check for ECC counts on the GPU before crash.

gcp-support-bot: Case GCP-4579123 update: engineering triage assigned. Requesting console serial log for gpu-eu3-052 and screenshots of dmesg around 12:02-12:10 UTC. ETA for initial findings: 2-4 hours.

kevin_oncall: I'm going to provision replacement hosts in eu-west-3 to restore dedicated capacity and then reprovision the faulty machines out of the rotation. Jamal, please coordinate reprovision and hardware replacement orders with cloud rep.

jamal_infra: Ordering spare hosts and scheduling reprovision. I've flagged the three hosts for rebuild and attached a note to the ticket to preserve dmesg/serial logs for RCA. Also capturing kernel oops coredumps: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq; echo c > /proc/sysrq-trigger` (we have crashkernel configured).

priya_sre: Also saving a subset of NVML logs from the pods around the event. Example NVML error visible in container logs:
```
E NVIDIA-SMI: GPU 0: Xid (13) GPU page fault 0x5c (PCIE)
E NVIDIA-SMI: A GPU restart is required for device functionality
```

emily_se: For customer comms, we'll include timeline, mitigation steps, and next steps (GCP investigation + full RCA). Draft ready for review: will send to legal and customer success for sign-off.

kevin_oncall: Handoff to second shift: Summary: three hosts in eu-west-3 saw bursty PCIe AER then kernel panic/reboot leading to pod restarts and customer 5xxs. Mitigation: drained and tainted hosts, routed traffic away, opened GCP case GCP-4579123, ordering reprovision. Tasks for next on-call: follow GCP findings, validate replacement hosts' firmware/BIOS/bridge firmware, re-run stress test on new hosts before returning to pool, and prepare follow-up comms.

sasha_reliability: I'll own the RCA doc. Items I'm tracking: log collection (dmesg, serial, nvidia logs), firmware versions (BIOS, BMC, PCIe bridge), network fabric flaps, and any historical error counts on those hosts. Expecting to produce a preliminary RCA within 48 hours depending on GCP info.

kevin_oncall: Thanks team. If GCP finds hardware faults we'll request replacement parts and confirm isolation procedures. I'll leave runbook notes in the incident channel and mark this thread as active-handoff.

priya_sre: Leaving a final note: remember to check for residual KV cache inconsistencies after pod restarts — some inference sessions might have dropped context. Adding a quick sweep job to invalidate caches for affected models.

emily_se: Customer comms sent to affected accounts (CUE: high-touch) at 13:10 UTC.

gcp-support-bot: Update on case GCP-4579123: engineering reports repeated corrected PCIe errors followed by uncorrectable ECC on GPU -> host reboot. They requested permission to move VMs to a new host and run diagnostic firmware updates. Please approve if you want them to proceed.

kevin_oncall: Approve. Jamal, please coordinate with the rep and confirm replacement host IDs once done.

jamal_infra: Approved and scheduled. Will post replacement IDs and reprovision timeline in this thread when complete.

sasha_reliability: Noted. Closing the active handoff — second shift please continue the RCA and post interim findings here. We'll produce a full postmortem and remediation plan after provider analysis. :white_check_mark:

kevin_oncall: Handoff complete. Leaving on-call.

-- end of thread --
